                               State of Rhode Island




JANUARY SESSION of the General Assembly begun and held at the State House in the City
of Providence on Tuesday, the Sixth day of January in the year of Our Lord Two Thousand
and Twenty Six.

 Volume 153, No. 42            Wednesday, June 10, 2026           Forty-Second Legislative Day

                                      CALL TO ORDER

The Senate meets pursuant to recess and is called to order by The Honorable Valarie J. Lawson,
President of the Senate, at 4:05 o’clock P.M.

                                         ROLL CALL

The roll is called and a quorum is declared present with 38 Senators present and 0 Senator absent
as follows:

PRESENT –38: The Honorable President Valarie J. Lawson, Senators Acosta, Appollonio, Bell,
Bissaillon, Britto, Burke, Ciccone, de la Cruz, DiMario, Dimitri, DiPalma, Euer, Famiglietti,
Felag, Gallo, Gu, Kallman, LaMountain, Lauria, Mack, McKenney, Morgan, Murray, Paolino,
Patalano, Pearson, Quezada, Raptakis, Rogers, Sosnowski, Thompson, Tikoian, Ujifusa, Urso,
Valverde, and Vargas, Zurier.

ABSENT – 0:

The Honorable President, by unanimous consent, presents Senator Felag to deliver the
invocation.


                       PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE TO THE FLAG

The Honorable President, by unanimous consent, presents Senator Felag to lead the Senate in the
pledge of allegiance to the flag.

                              IMMEDIATE CONSIDERATION

Senate Resolution No. 3371
BY LaMountain
ENTITLED, SENATE RESOLUTION HONORING THRIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, INC.
ON THE OCCASION OF ITS 50TH ANNIVERSARY AND RECOGNIZING ITS ENDURING
IMPACT ON THE HEALTH AND WELL-BEING OF RHODE ISLANDERS
{LC6566/1}

Senator LaMountain requests unanimous consent for immediate consideration.

Unanimous consent for immediate consideration is granted.

Senator LaMountain moves passage, seconded by The Honorable President Valarie J. Lawson,
Senators Acosta, Appollonio, Bell, Britto, Burke, Ciccone, de la Cruz, DiMario, Dimitri,
DiPalma, Euer, Famiglietti, Felag, Gu, Kallman, Mack, McKenney, Murray, Paolino, Patalano,
Quezada, Rogers, Sosnowski, Thompson, Tikoian, Ujifusa, Urso, Valverde, and Vargas, Zurier.
The resolution is read and passed upon a voice vote.

3.     2026-S 2798
       BY Famiglietti
       ENTITLED, AN ACT RELATING TO PROPERTY -- RHODE ISLAND
       COORDINATE SYSTEM

        Committee on Environment & Agriculture recommends passage.
Senator Famiglietti moves passage of the act, seconded by Senators Acosta, Appollonio, Bell,
Britto, Burke, Ciccone, Dimitri, DiPalma, Felag, Gallo, Kallman, LaMountain, Lauria, Mack,
McKenney, Murray, Patalano, Raptakis, Sosnowski, Tikoian, Urso, Zurier.

Senator Bell offers the following written motion to amend:
S.J. -- 14                                     JOURNAL                     Wednesday, June 10, 2026


                                        FLOOR AMENDMENT

                                                    TO

                                              2026 -- S 2798



         AN ACT RELATING TO PROPERTY -- RHODE ISLAND COORDINATE SYSTEM

Madam President:

        I hereby move to amend 2026 -- S 2798, entitled “AN ACT RELATING TO PROPERTY --

RHODE ISLAND COORDINATE SYSTEM”, as follows:

        1. On page 1, line 15, by striking the language “state”.

        2. On page 4, line 10, by deleting the language “used for projects commenced” and inserting in

place thereof the language “the exclusive Rhode Island coordinate system”.

3. On page 4, line 14, after the language "(a)", by deleting the language “The” and inserting in place

thereof the language “For the purposes of this chapter, the”.



Respectfully submitted,

Senator Bell



========
LC005443/3
========


The motion to amend prevails upon a roll call vote with 37 Senators voting in the affirmative, 0 Senator
voting in the negative as follows:

Burke, Ciccone, de la Cruz, DiMario, Dimitri, DiPalma, Euer, Famiglietti, Felag, Gallo, Gu, Kallman,
LaMountain, Lauria, Mack, McKenney, Morgan, Murray, Paolino, Patalano, Quezada, Pearson, Raptakis,
Rogers, Sosnowski, Thompson, Tikoian, Ujifusa, Urso, Valverde, and Vargas, Zurier.

NAYS – 0:

       BY Burke

       PROJECT LABOR AGREEMENTS

Senator Burke offers the following written motion to amend:

                                    FLOOR AMENDMENT
                                               TO
                                 2026 -- S 2735 SUBSTITUTE A

AN ACT RELATING TO PUBLIC PROPERTY AND WORKS -- PROJECT LABOR AGREEMENTS
Madam President:
        I hereby move to amend 2026 -- S 2735 SUBSTITUTE A, entitled “AN ACT RELATING
TO PUBLIC PROPERTY AND WORKS -- PROJECT LABOR AGREEMENTS”, as follows:
        1. On page 1, in the title of the Act, by deleting the language "PROJECT LABOR
AGREEMENTS", and by inserting in place thereof the language "STATE PURCHASES".
        2. On page 2, line 1, by deleting the language "the one hundred ten (110)" and by inserting
in place thereof the language "more than sixty (60)".
        3. On page 3, between lines 18 and 19, by inserting the language:
        "(1) Any determination not to use a PLA on a large-scale state public works project shall
be made by the chief procurement officer or an equivalent senior official of the state contracting
agency and include a detailed explanation of the reasons supporting the determination which shall
be reviewed by the agency's highest ranking official, who shall confirm or reverse the
determination in a written review decision."
        4. On page 3, line 19, by deleting the language "(1)" and by inserting in place thereof the

language "(2)".

       5. On page 3, lines 23 through 26, by deleting all language therein.

       6. On page 4, lines 6 through 21, by deleting all language therein and by inserting in place

thereof the language:

       "(c) For non-large-scale public works projects, a state contracting agency may, in its

discretion, require a project labor agreement to be incorporated into the contract specifications;
S.J. -- 24                                 JOURNAL                   Wednesday, June 10, 2026

provided that, such agreements are used in compliance with this section and that the PLA includes

the mandatory provisions specified herein."

       7. On page 5, line 7, by deleting the language "be construed to contravene any state or",

and by inserting in place thereof the language "contravene".

       8. On page 5, line 7, after the language "law or" by deleting the language "to".

       9. On page 6, between lines 23 and 24, by inserting the language

       "(1) Any determination not to use a PLA on a large-scale municipal public works project

shall be made by the chief procurement officer or an equivalent senior official of the municipal

contracting agency and include a detailed explanation of the reasons supporting the determination

which shall be reviewed by the agency's highest ranking official, who shall confirm or reverse the

determination in a written review decision."

       10. On page 6, line 24, by deleting the language "(1)", and by inserting in place thereof the

language "(2)".

       11. On page 6, lines 28 through 31, by deleting all language therein.

       12. On page 7, lines 11 through 26, by deleting all language therein and by inserting in

place thereof the language:

       "(c) For non-large-scale public works projects, a municipal contracting agency may, in its

discretion, require a project labor agreement to be incorporated into the contract specifications;

provided that, such agreements are used in compliance with this section and that the PLA includes

the mandatory provisions specified herein."

       13. On page 8, lines 6 and 7, by deleting the language "project workforce shall consist of

registered apprentices covered by apprenticeship agreements; and ", and by inserting in place

thereof the language "labor hours worked on the project be performed by apprentices in registered
S.J. -- 25                                    JOURNAL                      Wednesday, June 10, 2026

apprentice programs; and".

        14. On page 8, line 12, by deleting the language "be construed to contravene any state or",

and by inserting the language "contravene".

15. On page 8, line 12, after the language "law or" by deleting the language "to".



Respectfully submitted,

Senator CICCONE, III

Senator Euer offers the following written motion to amend:

                                     FLOOR AMENDMENT

                                                 TO

                                          2026 -- H 7437



      AN ACT RELATING TO MOTOR AND OTHER VEHICLES -- AUTOMATED TRAFFIC

                               VIOLATION MONETARY SYSTEMS

Madam President:

       I hereby move to amend 2026 -- H 7437, entitled “AN ACT RELATING TO MOTOR

AND OTHER VEHICLES -- AUTOMATED TRAFFIC VIOLATION MONETARY

SYSTEMS”, as follows:

       1. On page 2, between lines 12 and 13, by inserting the following language:

       "(f) Use of the images or video captured by an automated traffic violation monitoring

system shall be restricted to enforcement of the traffic violation and shall not be used to track

individuals or vehicles for any purpose. All recorded images or video shall be destroyed or retained

consistent with the provisions of § 31-41.2-8.

       (g) Absent a judicial warrant, the images, recordings, metadata, license plate information,

or other information collected by, or obtained from, an automated traffic violation monitoring
S.J. -- 32                                     JOURNAL                       Wednesday, June 10, 2026

system shall not be sold, shared, or transferred to any third parties, including other government

agencies, by the department of transportation or municipalities except for enforcement of the

traffic violation."

        1. On page 3, between lines 2 and 3, by inserting the following language:

        "(f) Use of the images or video captured by an automated traffic violation monitoring

system shall be restricted to enforcement of the traffic violation and shall not be used to track

individuals or vehicles for any purpose. All recorded images or video shall be destroyed or retained

consistent with the provisions of § 31-41.2-8.

(g) Absent a judicial warrant, the images, recordings, metadata, license plate information, or other

information collected by, or obtained from, an automated traffic violation monitoring system shall not be

sold, shared, or transferred to any third parties, including other government agencies, by the department

of transportation or municipalities except for enforcement of the traffic violation."



Respectfully submitted,

Senator Euer
